extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (Central Reexamination Unit) and practitioners preparing or responding to ex parte reexamination requests (patent owners, third‑party requesters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, evaluating, and processing requests and decisions for ex parte reexamination of U.S. patents, including what constitutes a "substantial new question of patentability" (SNQ), required contents of decisions/orders, procedural timing, and permissible grounds and evidence. Intended primarily for examiners but also informs practitioners responding to or filing requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of "old art" and multiple SNQ bases
rubrics_metrics.description: Where more than one SNQ is presented based solely on old art, the examiner would insert all such bases for SNQ. In bracket 3, for each basis identified in bracket 2, explain how and why that fact situation applies in the proceeding being acted on (e.g., old art is being presented/viewed in a new light or in a different way, in view of a material new argument or interpretation presented in the request).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples/authority: See Ex parte Chicago Rawhide Mfg. Co., 223 USPQ 351 (Bd. Pat. App. & Inter. 1984). This form paragraph is only used the first time the “already cited/considered” art is applied and is not repeated for the same art in subsequent Office actions. See MPEP § 2258.01 for use of “old art” in ordered reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior adverse Office decisions on same/substantially identical prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior decision adverse to the patentability of a claim by the Office based upon prior art patents or printed publications would usually mean that 'a substantially new question of patentability' is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: could arise from a reissue application abandoned after rejection of the claim and without disclaiming the patent claim. Examiner should consider such prior adverse Office decisions when determining whether SNQ is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior adverse reissue/final decisions based on non‑patent/non‑publication grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Any prior adverse final decision by the Director of the USPTO or the Board on an application seeking to reissue the same patent will be considered when determining whether a SNQ is present; however, to the extent such prior adverse final decision was based upon grounds other than patents or printed publications, it will not be a basis for determining whether a SNQ is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior adverse final decision is based on non‑patent grounds, it should not be relied upon as the basis for finding a SNQ under reexamination rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions in other cases involving same prior art (weight varies)
rubrics_metrics.description: While the Office will consider decisions involving substantially identical patents or printed publications in determining whether a SNQ is raised, the weight to be given such decisions will depend upon the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate contextual factors before assigning weight to decisions in other cases; do not treat them as automatically dispositive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of federal court decisions on SNQ (final validity, nonfinal, final invalidity)
rubrics_metrics.description: When considering whether prior art raises a SNQ, a final court decision of claim validity in view of the same or different prior art does not necessarily mean no SNQ is present because of differing standards of proof; factual findings may be accorded deference but the Office's determination is independent. A nonfinal holding of invalidity/unenforceability is not controlling. A final holding of invalidity or unenforceability after all appeals is controlling and a SNQ would not be present as to the claims finally held invalid or unenforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases cited: In re Swanson, 540 F.3d 1368 (Fed. Cir. 2008); In re Baxter Int’l, 678 F.3d 1357 (Fed. Cir. 2012); Ethicon v. Quigg, 849 F.2d 1422 (Fed. Cir. 1988). Bring unclear situations to Office of Patent Legal Administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims considered in deciding the request (claims in effect at time)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of the patent in effect at the time of the determination will be the basis for deciding whether a SNQ is present (37 CFR 1.515(a)). The Office's determination will generally be limited to review of the claim(s) for which reexamination was requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters must set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested (35 U.S.C. 302). If requester fails to apply the art to certain claims, requester is not statutorily entitled to reexamination of such claims. The Office may, in its discretion, reexamine claims not requested (35 U.S.C. 303(a)). If reexamination is ordered, the prosecution should be on the basis of the claims as amended by any copending reexamination or reissue proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of prior art the examiner may rely on
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination whether a SNQ is present can be based upon any prior art patents or printed publications; the examiner is not limited to the patents/publications relied upon in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may rely on (a) prior art cited in the request, (b) combination of art in the request and other art found elsewhere, or (c) entirely different patents/printed publications. Examiner may consider patents/publications of record from timely 37 CFR 1.501 submissions (compliant with 1.98). If additional art can be readily obtained to supply deficiencies, examiner may perform a limited targeted search where there is a reasonable likelihood of finding such art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to order reexamination must identify claims/issues, art, and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: If a SNQ is found, the determination will include an order for reexamination and the examiner’s decision will (A) identify all claims and issues, (B) identify the patents and/or printed publications relied on, and (C) provide a brief statement of the rationale supporting each new question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must identify at least one SNQ and explain how the prior art raises such a question. Examiner should, insofar as possible, indicate initial positions on all issues identified in the request to allow comment in the patent owner’s statement and requester’s reply. Prior art relied on should be listed on form PTO‑892 or equivalent; supply copies only where not previously supplied to the patent owner/requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision contents: six required points (A–F)
rubrics_metrics.description: As to each SNQ identified, the decision should point out: (A) the prior art patents/printed publications which add some new teaching as to at least one claim; (B) what that new teaching is; (C) the claims that the new teaching is directed to; (D) that the new teaching was not previously considered nor addressed in the prior examination or a final court holding; (E) that the new teaching is such that a reasonable examiner would consider it important in deciding to allow the claim; and (F) where raised or unclear, why the patent or publication is deemed to be available against the patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2247.01 for an example decision. In simple cases examiner may adopt requester’s reasons. If request indicates SNQ without stating claims unpatentable, language should state SNQ is raised as to specified claims rather than asserting unpatentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision should not decide patentability (only whether SNQ exists)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the decision on the request, the examiner will not decide, and no statement should be made as to, whether the claims are rejected over the patents and printed publications; the examiner only decides whether a SNQ exists to order reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include rejections or conclusions on patentability in the decision ordering reexamination; initial positions on issues may be indicated but not rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper grounds for reexamination (non‑patent/non‑publication issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments based on grounds not based on patents or printed publications (e.g., public use or sale, abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 102(c) for proceedings examined under the first‑to‑invent regime) are improper for reexamination and are not considered or commented upon (see 37 CFR 1.552(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requester raises such grounds, note them as improper and do not consider them in deciding whether a SNQ exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner statement and reply timing and procedural limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When reexamination is ordered, the patent owner will be given a reasonable period, not less than two months from the date the determination is mailed, to file a statement on the SNQ, including any amendment and new claims to propose. The requester may file a reply within two months from service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not permitted (provisions apply only to 'an applicant'); ex parte reexamination proceedings are conducted with special dispatch (35 U.S.C. 305; 37 CFR 1.550(a)). Extensions in ex parte reexamination are provided in 37 CFR 1.550(c). For EFS‑Web transmissions, follow 37 CFR 1.8 filing/timeliness requirements including certificate of transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs and correspondence handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 22.01 should be used at the beginning of each decision letter ('New Question of Patentability'); Form paragraph 22.73 should be used at the end ('Correspondence and Inquiry as to Office Actions'). The decision granting the request is made on a decision form and must set forth the time periods for the patent owner and requester to file their statement and any reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide contact information for correspondence; technical support staff and CRU handle printing/mailing and make copies of prior art not already supplied. Use form PTOL‑465 for transmittals to third‑party requesters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision denying request: required explanatory categories for each citation
rubrics_metrics.description: If no SNQ is found, the decision denying reexamination must indicate, for each patent and printed publication cited in the request, why the citation is: (A) cumulative to the teachings of the art cited in the earlier examination; (B) not available against the claims (e.g., date or not a publication); (C) not important to a reasonable examiner in deciding patentability even though not cumulative and available; or (D) one cited in the record and barred by guidelines in MPEP § 2242, subsection II.A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 22.02 ('No New Question of Patentability') should be used as the introductory paragraph in a denial. Examiner should also respond to the substance of each argument raised by the requester that is based on patents or printed publications. Improper non‑patent grounds should be noted as not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and mailing procedures for decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: After examiner prepares, proofreads, and signs the decision, the reexamination file and decision are given to CRU Legal Instrument Examiner for clerical processing. Technical support prints the heading and, if request made by third party, makes copies for both patent owner and requester of any prior art documents not already supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the decision is mailed to patent owner and any third party along with required prior art copies. Original signed decision and copy of prior art enclosed is made of record in the reexamination electronic file. Use PTOL‑465 transmittal when mailing to third‑party requester; annotate and scan concluded files as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art citations submitted after the order
rubrics_metrics.description: Any prior art citations under 37 CFR 1.501 submitted after the date of the decision on the order should be retained in a separate file by the CRU or Technology Center until the reexamination proceeding is concluded, at which time the prior art citation is entered of record on the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2206 for details. Do not immediately enter such post‑order citations into the patent record; keep separate until conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeking review of SNQ determinations (patent owner reconsideration and Board review)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may challenge the correctness of the decision to grant reexamination on the basis that there is no SNQ by requesting reconsideration of the examiner’s SNQ determination in a patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or in a response under 37 CFR 1.111. To preserve the right to Board review of the SNQ issue, the patent owner must first request reconsideration before the examiner and then present the SNQ issue in its appeal brief to the Board, clearly identifying where reconsideration was first requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner agrees no SNQ, prosecution terminates or reexamination order vacated. If examiner maintains SNQ, patent owner may exhaust reexamination remedies and seek Board review on appeal. For ex parte reexaminations ordered on/after June 25, 2010, failure to request reconsideration before examiner may forfeit Board SNQ review rights. See MPEP § 2274 for appeal process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to vacate reexamination order as ultra vires (37 CFR 1.181(a)(3)) — appropriate circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.181(a)(3) to vacate an ex parte reexamination order as 'ultra vires' should be rare and granted only where the USPTO acted in 'brazen defiance' of its statutory authorization. Appropriate circumstances include: (A) order is facially not based on prior art patents or printed publications; (B) all claims for which reexamination ordered were held invalid by a final decision of a Federal Court after all appeals; (C) reexamination was ordered for the wrong patent; or (D) reexamination was ordered based on a duplicate copy of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no right to petition as ultra vires if SNQ is based on reasons other than those urged by the requester. Petitions to vacate are delegated to the Director of the Central Reexamination Unit; third‑party requester may file a single opposition submission (must file within two weeks of service) and should notify CRU support staff upon intention to oppose. File oppositions preferably by facsimile when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition from denial of request and CRU Director review
rubrics_metrics.description: If a requester seeks review of an examiner’s denial of reexamination under 37 CFR 1.515(c), the petition must be filed within one month of the mailing date and comply with 1.181(b). The CRU Director will review the examiner’s determination de novo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition is granted, CRU Director's decision includes a two‑month period for owner to file a statement under 37 CFR 1.530 and the file is returned for reassignment (reassignment is the general rule). If no petition or petition denied, determination is final and nonappealable (35 U.S.C. 303(c); 37 CFR 1.515(c)). Reassignment exceptions only in extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference and signatures on decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner will prepare for and set up a panel review conference per MPEP § 2271.01 to discuss issuance of the decision on the request. If the conference confirms the examiner’s preliminary decision to grant or deny reexamination, the decision will be completed and signed by the examiner, with two or more other conferees initialing the action to indicate their presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After signatures, examiner hand‑carries decision to CRU support staff for processing and mailing. Examiner may prepare initial Office action accompanying the decision either before or after the conference and revise as needed. If CRU SPRS believes another Art Unit should examine the file, follow transfer procedures in MPEP § 2237.
